# Released Meeting recording and desktop ownership

The immutable reference remains v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. The additional [joined recording fixture](../../../mluva-workflows/tests/fixtures/released-meeting-session.json), SHA-256 `7f0a574c51aedb3e2f264e807651931376c94dc63456118a1e31ab9bcd669ab3`, comes from fourteen transactions through the actual released PipeWireMeetingRecorder, WAV mixing, MeetingWorkflow and ElevenLabs HTTP client. The [desktop owner fixture](released-meeting-controller.json), SHA-256 `3108041f667ff2e8b0aec6ef583291e6b15bbfa33714bd87f9861cb549fbdc51`, comes from nine actual released MluvaApplication Meeting workflows/47 GTK states. Each external observer checks all imported application module bytes against the reference commit. Native checks consume these frozen outputs without invoking an interpreter.

MeetingRecorder owns both external capture processes and the staging/final audio on one dedicated worker. Stop/mixing never executes on the GTK context. Explicit transfer preserves indexed/recoverable audio; closing or dropping an untransferred result erases it. Session construction freezes the identifier, wall timestamp and privacy, requires persistent audio to use its archive directory, and rejects a storage/privacy mismatch. Incognito uses the actual native memory store and cleanup helper. Every capture/retry creates a fresh HTTP transport from the readiness owner's credential/path snapshot, so a completed or closed client cannot disable the next operation.

The joined recording check matches released WAV/provenance/warning/duration results, exact uploaded bytes/fields, portable records, private file/index bytes and permissions, successful retention, recognition/index failures, Incognito erasure and cancellation before Stop. It includes all five previously frozen audio cases in retained and Incognito forms. Additional native faults abort a slow Stop caller while timers keep running, preserve an unowned destination collision, and close sessions during slow finalization or a delayed actual HTTP response in both privacy modes. They reap both processes, erase untransferred audio and memory staging, leave no archive index, and reject terminal phase/index publication after close.

MeetingController now owns the real MeetingPage and joins it to ApplicationServices, CapturePage and CapturePreferences. The explicitly executed private GTK check matches normal recording, microphone/system fallback warnings, neither-source failure, Incognito completion/failure, failed retained recognition followed by explicit retry, failed index/manual transcript recovery and cancellation. It compares the actual buttons, selective capture/settings locks, frozen privacy summary, Meeting-only status messages, private archive/audio, content-free diagnostic stages, processing/retry/delete guards and both surfaces' return to idle. Processing is locked synchronously before dispatch, preventing repeated Stop from launching another completion. Capture/retry and filesystem/provider work execute on the background runtime; weak/owned-session checks prevent late UI callbacks after exit. The explicit shutdown task waits for the session/retry owner and must be awaited by the eventual root application before Quit.

Generated UUIDs, portable-record timestamps and their filename/path appearances are normalized. At in-flight processing/retry snapshots, external-process active state, finalization file inventory and diagnostic inventory are marked `in-flight`: their asynchronous publication order is not a stable snapshot boundary. Their exact final audio, record/index and diagnostic results are checked at terminal states; recording snapshots also compare the source files and ready diagnostic. Other fields/messages remain literal. The desktop test controls only the external PCM/HTTP peers and unrelated parent ports; the actual released application methods and actual native owner perform capture/Stop/retry/cancel/delete-guard logic. The parent window, capture provider, review and key owners are not assembled as a full application in this check.

Reproduce from the repository root with scratch under `tmp/`:

```sh
cargo build --locked -p mluva-audio --bin audio-fixture-peer --bin mluva-audio-cleanup
cargo test --locked -p mluva-audio --test audio_contracts
cargo test --locked -p mluva-workflows --test meeting
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/native-meeting-owner -- \
  cargo test --locked -p mluva-gtk --test meeting_controller -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture
```

Desktop comparisons isolate display, HOME/XDG, session/accessibility buses, network/PID/mount namespaces and input/audio/GPU nodes. Only synthetic PCM, synthetic credentials and owned loopback providers are used. Source observers/raw logs stay ignored scratch; fixture binaries are not selected by distribution. No host microphone/input/focus, real account/content upload or installed configuration is used.

This is bounded owner integration, not complete application or Meeting acceptance. Root window/services/Settings reconfiguration, physical microphone/system audio and keys, complete pending-review/History/recovery workflows, broader accessibility/scales, final packaging/Python removal and same-machine performance remain required. All complete-workflow matrix rows stay Pending. No complete runnable native app or Rust install/merge/release is claimed; the verified installed app/widget remain 1.6.0 and the full Rust goal remains active.
